A counterexample to the conjecture of Brešar, Bujtás, Gologranc, Klavžar, Košmrlj, Patkós, Tuza and
Vizer (Electron. J. Combin. 23(4) (2016), #P4.34, Conjecture 22) that the Grundy domination number is
multiplicative on strong products: γ_gr(K_{2,2,2}) = 2, γ_gr(H_21) = 10, and γ_gr(K_{2,2,2} ⊠ H_21) ≥ 21,
where u and v are adjacent in H_21 when |u − v| ≡ 2 (mod 3). The same construction fails the
conjecture for 21 ≤ N ≤ 63, with ratio up to 21/16, and also with circulant second factors.

Attached: the paper (PDF), its LaTeX source with the figures as PNG, and the arXiv tarball. The
repository contains the Lean 4 proof of the counterexample (25 theorems, standard axioms only), the C
and Python checks, and the dated priority check.

Author: Deep Bhattacharjee (ORCID 0000-0003-0466-750X).
